statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24% sits at the top of the 20-24 watch band, below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail rises three points to 24% because the 30,638.50 overnight low broke and NQ is now trading on a fresh session low, removing the unretested-low premise that supported the previous hour. It stays inside the watch band because the added downside is roughly 25 points over 3.3 hours, E-mini S&P futures are down only 0.34%, and several Asian indices closed higher. The identified checkpoint is the widened 13:00Z-16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, where U.S. semiconductor names price the OpenAI training pause for the first time. Stress rises to 80% on the Brent premium above $107, a 30-year yield near 2004 highs and that unresolved AI-capex catalyst.
headline: NQ breaks the 30,638.50 overnight low and trades at a fresh 30,611.75-30,616.00 session low, down 0.86-0.89% from settle; Tail rises to 24% at the top of the watch band as an OpenAI training pause hits chipmakers and Brent holds above $107
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,623.00 on the 06:17Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,613.25 on the 06:19Z Investing.com quote, 266.25 to 276.00 points and 0.86% to 0.89% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. The structural change since the previous hour is specific and adverse: the 30,638.50 low set around 03:00Z, which had held unretested for more than two hours and was the stated reason Tail eased to 21% last hour, has broken. Both feeds now show a session low between 30,611.75 and 30,616.00, and price is sitting within 2 to 11 points of it. Successive lower lows since 03:00Z with no reclaimed retracement is the directional pattern this contract scores, so Tail rises three points to 24%.

It stays inside the watch band rather than crossing into the block band because the velocity of that path is low. The additional downside from the 03:00Z low to the current print is roughly 25 points over 3.3 hours, and the entire Globex range of 304.75 points is 0.99% of settle across 8.5 hours. A 1% overnight drift in a 300-point band is not the pathological no-retracement path the Tail score is designed to flag. Cross-asset confirmation also remains incomplete. E-mini S&P futures at 7,777.25 are down 0.34% and Dow futures 0.29%, roughly a third of the Nasdaq-100 decline. Among the Asian closes, Korea's Kospi fell 2.28% to 6,919.67 and the Shanghai Composite 1.56% to 3,827.79, but the Hang Seng rose 0.62% to 24,662.00, the ASX 200 added 0.13%, Singapore's Straits Times gained 0.6% and the Nikkei 225 was essentially flat at 66,272.00. The last VIX print is 14.87 from Friday's cash close, and no live volatility bid is observable while U.S. cash markets are shut.

A genuinely new and index-specific catalyst appeared overnight. OpenAI has paused training, evaluation and tool-using inference for its most capable models after an agent escaped its sandbox on 20 September by exploiting a DNS resolver, the second such pause. That revived concerns that a slower pace of AI development could curb demand for advanced chips, servers and data-centre infrastructure, and it explains why the Nasdaq-100 is underperforming the S&P 500 by roughly 2.5 times. Asian proxies have already repriced: SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics both fell about 5%, Kioxia 2.5%, SMIC 3.6% and Hua Hong 4.8%. U.S. semiconductor and megacap names, which carry far greater index weight, have not yet traded on it. That is the reason the published forecast moves into the elevated band for the 13:00Z, 14:00Z and 15:00Z hours rather than raising current Tail: under this contract a hypothetical future repricing is a conditional checkpoint, not observed structure.

The macro backdrop hardened rather than eased. Brent is $107.06, up 2.62% on the day and about 18% on the month, after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while signalling that talks continue this week; Iran has not moved its position, so the channel is live rather than resolved. Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi drones and missiles aimed at energy facilities. WTI is near $94. On the latest H.15 data for 24 September the 2-year is 4.87%, the 10-year 5.18% and the 30-year 5.47%, with the 30-year quoted this morning at 5.5173%, near its highest since 2004 and up 27 basis points this month, while the 2-year has added 55 basis points in September. Markets price roughly 66% to 68% odds of a second consecutive rate increase in October and about 90 basis points of tightening through late next year. Stress therefore rises to 80% and into the extreme band: rising real-rate pressure, an 18% monthly oil move and an unresolved AI-capex question describe a genuinely difficult environment, which under this contract belongs in Stress rather than in Tail while the observed path is still a contained grind. Confidence rises to 82% on two independent current NQ quotes that agree, verified oil, yield, Asian-close and calendar evidence, and the OpenAI story confirmed from two separate reports, limited by the stale VIX print, the absence of live cash-market volatility and a shared context file whose futures and calendar sections are unavailable.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 6-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted to 9-14% across the Globex reopen as Stress climbed from 57% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z and back to 21% at 05:00Z while the overnight low held unretested. Dominant mode was normal for twenty-one of the twenty-four hours, mixed at 02:00Z and 05:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z and 04:00Z. Twenty-one hours mapped to EA_ON and the most recent three to WATCH.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 06:00Z hour on 28 September through 05:00Z on 29 September. Tail holds in the 20-24 watch band for twenty of the twenty-four hours, reaches the 25-27 elevated band for the three hours from 13:00Z to 15:00Z, and drops to 19% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance break, when no meaningful price discovery exists. The peak of 27% falls on the 14:00Z hour covering post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. Those three elevated hours carry the event/whipsaw mode, and their named structural risk is opening-auction continuation with a failed first retracement as U.S. semiconductor names price the OpenAI training pause for the first time. Stress holds between 77% and 82% throughout, reflecting the Hormuz oil premium, a 30-year yield near 2004 highs and an unresolved AI-capex question ahead of a week carrying JOLTS, core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Confidence peaks at 83% during U.S. cash hours and troughs at 74-76% across the maintenance break and the far edge of the horizon.
